answer.evidence: The width profile is 6, 8, 8, then 10 from row 3 to row 29. The top is only chamfered at its upper corners, and the cap has the same width as the shaft (10 against 10). It does not widen and then narrow again, so there is no ellipse and no overhang. The cap in rows 1-7 is a flat-shaded front face with a highlight and a dark outline row at row 8. It has no front-edge line or eave shadow that would mark a horizontal surface. The sign panel (rows 9-18) and the lower shaft (rows 20-27) are also vertical faces. The whole object is a front elevation, like the 'column: flat band cap' reference marked wrong.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a slim sign post: a light grey cylindrical pole with a dark cap and a dark-blue base, plus a yellow-orange panel showing the number 2. It has about 4 lightness steps on the pole (highlight, light, mid, dark) and its outline is a dark tinted blue-grey, not neutral (0% near-neutral edge pixels, matching the references). The measured 12 visible tones per tile equals kiosk-a (12) and exceeds bus-shelter-a (6), though it is below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 14%, above kiosk-a and vending-a (0%) and above bus-shelter-a (9%), so it has a few flat areas, mainly on the pole body and the sign panel. Next to the references it looks somewhat thinner and simpler than kiosk-a and vending-a, with less grain and fewer shading steps. Because the object is thin and sparse, this is acceptable by eye, but it is still a little thin beside the richest references. It is on par with bus-shelter-a, which is itself simple, so the candidate is not a sticker-like outlier.
